s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal mass with variable growth pattern in a patient with history of plasma cell myeloma
salient_findings: Lesion in the right hepatic lobe with increased SUVmax on PET/CT
Lesion in segment VI with restricted diffusion on MRI
Variable lesion size over time, initially decreasing then enlarging
key_facts: Patient has IgG kappa plasma cell myeloma
Patient has undergone multiple chemotherapy regimens
Patient has undergone two autologous stem-cell transplants
Patient has undergone thalidomide maintenance and focal bone radiotherapy
Patient is asymptomatic with stable vital signs
No hepatosplenomegaly on examination
Liver function tests are within normal limits
PET/CT showed a 35 mm lesion in the right hepatic lobe with SUVmax of 6.1
MRI showed a 17 mm lesion in segment VI with moderately increased T2 signal and decreased T1 signal
Lesion has weak heterogeneous contrast enhancement and restricted diffusion on MRI
Lesion size decreased to 10 mm then enlarged to 57 × 46 mm over time

shortlist.label: Plasma cell myeloma hepatic involvement
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has history of IgG kappa plasma cell myeloma and imaging shows a lesion with characteristics concerning for malignant involvement

shortlist.label: Extramedullary plasmacytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has history of plasma cell myeloma and lesion characteristics are consistent with a possible extramedullary plasmacytoma

shortlist.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lesion characteristics on imaging, such as weak heterogeneous contrast enhancement and restricted diffusion, are concerning for a primary liver malignancy

shortlist.label: Metastatic disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has history of multiple chemotherapy regimens and autologous stem-cell transplants, increasing the risk of secondary malignancies

shortlist.label: Hepatic lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Lesion characteristics and patient's history of immunosuppression increase the risk of lymphoma

raw.rationale: The patient's history of IgG kappa plasma cell myeloma and the presence of a liver lesion with characteristics suggestive of malignancy on imaging studies, along with the fluctuation in lesion size, are most consistent with hepatic involvement of the patient's known plasma cell myeloma.

rejected.label: Extramedullary plasmacytoma
rejected.why: While possible, the presence of a solitary lesion in the liver without other evidence of extramedullary disease makes this less likely.

rejected.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
rejected.why: Normal liver function tests and the absence of hepatosplenomegaly make primary liver cancer less likely.

rejected.label: Metastatic disease
rejected.why: The patient's history of myeloma and the characteristics of the liver lesion make metastatic disease from another primary less likely.

rejected.label: Hepatic lymphoma
rejected.why: There is no other evidence to suggest lymphoma, and the patient's known history of myeloma makes this diagnosis less likely.
